findings.title: Rollback now reverses user txs while later :fix txs on the same entities stay applied, so the reversal can be left half done.
findings.body:
The old code reversed every tx in `rejected-and-after` in reverse order. That meant a `:fix` that came after a rejected user tx was undone first, and the user tx's reversed datoms then hit the values they expected. Now every `:fix` is skipped, including later ones that were not rejected and that rewrote `:block/order` on blocks the rejected user tx created or moved.

Example trigger: the user inserts a block whose order collides with a sibling. `repair-applied-txs!` queues a `:fix` that changes the new block's order from X to Y. The server then rejects the insert. Reversing the insert retracts `[e :block/order X]`, which does nothing because the current value is Y, and retracts the block's other attributes. The result is an orphan entity that has only `:block/order Y`, plus a pending `:fix` that points at a block that no longer exists.

Fix: only keep a `:fix` applied when it is itself rejected and no earlier non-fix tx in the window is reversed. Otherwise, keep reversing every tx that comes after a reversed user tx, as before. For example, skip `:fix` txs only up to the first non-fix tx in `rejected-and-after`. I could not see `reverse-local-txs!`, so I could not confirm exactly what it emits.
